title: The $6 Billion Job Interview
event: 29 Oct 2026: hackers took about $6.3 billion from Binance's hot wallets in under four hours, the biggest crypto theft on record. Binance says the way in was a fake job interview: fake recruiters won an engineer's trust and a fake 'CEO' sent a coding test that hid malware. About $2.85 billion was frozen; Binance says it covered customers' losses; the FBI attributes it to North Korea, which denies it. 18-19 Nov 2026: an Abu Dhabi court (ADGM) granted a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order that can be served on the blockchain, while laundering through thousands of wallets ramps up

title: The Money on Trial
event: Mon 23 Nov 2026: the US Justice Department files a civil forfeiture complaint in a Washington, D.C., federal court against about $1.17bn of USDC stolen in the 29 Oct 2026 Binance hack (about $6.3bn, the biggest crypto theft on record; the FBI blames North Korea, which denies it). In such a case the money itself is the defendant and no one has to be charged. Circle has frozen the USDC but cannot move the original tokens, so it agreed to issue new USDC to the US if the court orders forfeiture. Bitcoin and ether cannot be frozen: the rest was scattered across 27,000+ wallets and even home-made meme coins; trackers say more than $2bn still sits in wallets tied to the theft (Elliptic, 23 Nov)
angle: the chase: why the US is suing the money itself (civil forfeiture of about $1.17bn of frozen USDC, filed 23 Nov 2026), how a frozen coin gets back (Circle issues new USDC if a judge orders it), and why bitcoin and ether can't be frozen (27,000+ wallets, home-made meme coins, more than $2bn still in theft-linked wallets)

title: The Call Nobody Wants
event: Week to Fri 20 Nov 2026: Taiwan's TAIEX falls 17.5% (7,641.83 points), its worst week in more than 30 years (Reuters: since 1990; Bloomberg: 35 years); the main board loses NT$24.97 trillion of market value (NT$143.07tn to NT$118.10tn, TWSE figures via Taiwanese press), about US$760 billion at NT$32.94 per US$ (Reuters/LSEG: US$1.12tn since the 6 Oct record). Many had bought with borrowed money (40% own, 60% lent; a margin call at 78% of the price, two business days to top up, then a forced sale): margin calls hit a record 6,462 accounts on 20 Nov (719 on 18 Nov), forced sales and the one-day fall in margin loans were records too. TWSE lowered the call line from 130% to 120% from Tue 24 Nov and cancelled earlier calls (FSC also curbed short selling; the NT$500bn fund bought shares). Tue 24 Nov, after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang: +8.99% (+3,310.46 points), the biggest one-day point gain on record; Wed 25 Nov: down as much as 3,440.45 points (8.6%), the second-largest intraday point loss, closing 4.8% lower at 38,195.43
angle: Taiwan's crash and the mechanism of margin calls: how borrowed money turned a fall into the worst week in over 30 years (buy with 40 of your own and 60 borrowed, a fall of about a fifth brings the lender's call, pay within two days or it sells for you; forced selling feeds more calls), the record margin calls and record unwind of margin loans, the response (short-selling ban, state fund, brokers moving the margin-call line from 130% to 120%), and the latest twist (record one-day gain on 24 Nov, then another plunge on 25 Nov)

title: The Nervous Lenders
event: Tue 24 Nov 2026, the day after Nvidia jumped 31.5% on Jensen Huang's return: the cost of insuring AI companies' debt against default (five-year credit default swaps) hits records (Reuters, S&P Global Market Intelligence: Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX, CoreWeave). Oracle 356 bps, about $3.56 a year to insure $100 of its debt (Reuters; CNBC 355.68); CoreWeave 1,314 bps (Reuters; FactSet 1,332; CNBC over 1,200), about $13 per $100, its 9.75% 2031 bond yielding over 17% (CNBC) after falling to 76.6 cents on the dollar (Bloomberg). title: The Dice Nobody Rolled
event: The Coldcard seed flaw: from firmware of March 2021 until 30 Jul 2026, Coinkite's Coldcard hardware wallets silently made their wallet secrets (seeds) with a predictable software generator instead of the chip's hardware random number generator; from 29-30 Jul 2026 thieves rebuilt the keys on their own computers and swept bitcoin from wallets that never went online (594 BTC in 25 minutes; over $100 million in all); Coinkite's 18-page postmortem (dated 23 Nov, published 24 Nov 2026) counts 1,778.84 BTC from 8,600+ addresses (Galaxy Research), 242 customer accounts reporting losses, at least 15 reviews that missed it, and no compensation decision yet
story: The Coldcard bitcoin wallet seed flaw (2026)
angle: the mechanism and the latest twist: how you rob a wallet that never goes online (its secret was supposed to come from pure chance, but for five years it came from a guessable recipe, so thieves rebuilt the secrets at home), why at least 15 reviews missed it (the checks confirmed the random-number hardware was there, never that the secrets used it), and the maker's postmortem of 24 Nov 2026 (about 1,779 BTC from 8,600+ addresses, 242 customers, no compensation decision yet); no advice

title: The Slow Billions

title: The 12-Second Trap
event: Mon 16 Nov 2026: US District Judge Jessica Clarke (Manhattan) grants a judgment of acquittal to MIT-educated brothers Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, closing the first US criminal case over MEV without a second trial. Prosecutors had said that in April 2023 the brothers took about $25 million of crypto from Ethereum 'sandwich' trading bots in about 12 seconds: bait trades lured the bots, then a flaw in MEV-Boost relay software showed the brothers the block before it was locked, and they swapped the bait for their own sells. Charged May 2024 (wire fraud, conspiracy, money laundering, up to 20 years each); first trial ended in a mistrial in Nov 2025 after the jury deadlocked. The judge found no material misrepresentation proven (Ethereum is 'a trustless, highly adversarial environment with no terms of use'; the question was 'not whether the Peraire-Buenos' conduct was right or moral').

angle: what happened + the mechanism + the latest twist: how about $25 million moved from trading robots to two brothers in 12 seconds (sandwich bots that jump in front of other people's trades were baited, then a flaw in the software that seals each block showed the brothers the robots' orders early and they swapped in their own sells), why prosecutors called it fraud, and the twist: after a 2025 mistrial, Judge Jessica Clarke acquitted them on 16 Nov 2026 because no lie was proven ('no terms of use'; 'not whether ... right or moral'); case closed; no advice

title: The Boss Who Wasn't There
event: Thu 5 Nov 2026 (US time): Manhattan federal prosecutors unseal an indictment charging Jacob Soall (41), Sharon Hazan (54) and Guy Sheetrit (42), arrested in Spain (17 Jun, 5 Aug 2026) and the UK (7 Sep 2026), with wire fraud, aggravated identity theft and money laundering. Prosecutors say that between July 2024 and February 2026 they used AI to mimic companies' CEOs (the voice, sometimes the face) on calls about a 'confidential financial transaction', then posed as lawyers at large international law firms (a 'Lawyer Call' script told staff not to discuss it with colleagues), getting finance staff to wire at least $129 million to bank accounts in nine countries, then turned it into crypto. Victims include hospital systems in Missouri and California, a Rhode Island bank, a UK fintech (about $11.6 million), a Massachusetts mutual fund company and a Florida pet food company. The charges are accusations; the men are presumed innocent (Sheetrit's lawyers say he had no involvement). Extradition pending.
